summary: The PIR motion sensor video is the clear winner, getting far more views, likes, shares and saves than anything else, mostly on Instagram. Other Hindi videos get small but steady Instagram views and almost nothing on YouTube, so YouTube is not picking them up yet. The English Arduino video got decent YouTube views but zero on Instagram, and the data is too small to say the language is the cause.
winningPattern: A familiar sensor or everyday device explained as a surprising myth-buster in Hindi (Hinglish), with a title that opens with a bold claim or a question ('X Aapko Dekhta Nahi!', 'Kaise Kaam Karta Hai?'), a thinking emoji and #shorts. It performs best on Instagram Reels, with YouTube a smaller second channel. Subjects people meet daily (motion detection, phones, doors) beat abstract ones.
doMore: Open every title with a surprising claim or myth about a sensor people use daily, like the PIR one.
Make Instagram the main platform and post there first, since it brings about 3x the views of YouTube.
Ask viewers to share and save in the last line, such as 'Dost ko bhejo jo sochta hai...', because shares and saves are what the score rewards.
Pair each sensor topic with a real maker use, such as 'ise Arduino se banao', to attract students and makers.
Rewatch the PIR video to find what worked (first 2 seconds, pacing, visuals) and copy that structure into the next five videos.
stopDoing: Stop using vague or weak-hook topics like street light or TV remote with a plain question title and no surprise.
Stop posting English-only videos to a channel whose audience responds in Hindi unless you run a proper test with a Hindi version of the same topic.
